main.claim: Upload a PDF, type a question, and get a short answer taken only from that PDF, with the page number when the tool can find it. Free: 3 questions a day, no account, no app to install.

sections.heading: How to chat with a PDF
sections.body:
1. Open this page.
2. Choose your PDF. The file can be up to 15 MB.
3. Type your question in the chat box and send it.
4. Read the answer. It appears in about 1 to 3 seconds.
5. Copy the answer with one click, or ask the next question.

sections.heading: What to ask
sections.body:
Ask about one thing at a time. A question with a clear target gets a clear answer.

- Facts: "What is the refund period in this contract?"
- Summaries of one section: "Summarize the methods section in five sentences."
- Definitions: "What does the report mean by net margin?"
- Lists: "List every date in this schedule."
- Locations: "Which page explains the warranty?"

If you name a section, chapter or topic from the PDF, the answer is usually more exact.

sections.heading: What the answers are based on
sections.body:
The tool answers from the PDF you uploaded. It does not browse the web or use other documents. When the PDF does not contain the answer, the tool says so instead of guessing.

When the answer matters, open the page the tool names and read the text yourself. A short answer can leave out a condition, an exception or a date that appears elsewhere in the file. Read the surrounding paragraph before you act on it.

sections.heading: Limits to know about
sections.body:
- **File type:** PDF only. For a Word or PowerPoint file, save it as a PDF first.
- **File size:** up to 15 MB per file.
- **Free use:** 3 questions a day. Leave an email to get 3 more that day. No account is needed for the first 3.
- **AI model:** the answers come from Google Gemini, running on Lazur's servers.

The free limits are set by Lazur and can change. The limits above are the ones the tool shows today.

If you hit the daily limit, the tool tells you. Your uploaded file and your question do not change the limit, so you can come back the next day and start again with the same PDF.

sections.heading: Tips for better answers
sections.body:
Short questions with a clear subject work best. Ask for the page number if you need to check the source. If the first answer is too general, ask again and name the part of the PDF you care about. For a long report, ask about one chapter at a time instead of the whole file at once.

A good first question is one you already know the answer to. That tells you quickly whether the tool reads the file the way you expect, before you rely on it for something new.

pages.title: Chat with PDF Tutorial: Ask Your PDF a Question | Lazur
pages.description: A short chat with PDF tutorial: upload your file, ask a question, and get an answer from the page in seconds. Free, no account, works in your browser.
pages.claim: Drop a PDF of up to 15 MB onto this page, type your question, and the answer appears in about 1 to 3 seconds, based only on that file. Free, with no account and nothing to install.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.body:
1. Open this page on your computer or phone.
2. Click the upload area and choose your PDF, or drag the file onto it.
3. Wait for the file to load. Then type a question in the chat box.
4. Send the question. The answer appears under it.
5. Read the answer. If the tool names a page, open that page in your PDF viewer to check the text.
6. Click the copy button to copy the answer, or ask a follow-up question.

You can ask as many follow-up questions as your daily free limit allows. Each question uses one of them.

sections.heading: A tutorial for a 20-page report
sections.body:
Say you have a 20-page annual report and need the total revenue. Upload the report and ask: "What was total revenue for the year?" The answer gives the figure and, when it can find it, the page where the figure appears.

Now ask a second question that depends on the first: "How did that compare with last year?" Asking follow-ups in the same chat keeps your context, so you do not have to repeat the file or the subject.

When you are done with a file, you can upload a different one and start a new set of questions. Copy any answer you want to keep before you do, because the answer is not saved for you on the page.

For a longer file, ask about one part at a time. "Summarize the risks section" gives a tighter answer than "Summarize everything."

sections.heading: When the answer is wrong or missing
sections.body:
If the tool says the PDF does not contain the answer, the information may be in an image, a table the tool cannot read well, or a different section than you expected. Try a shorter question with a keyword from the file, such as a heading or a name.

If the answer seems wrong, ask the same question in a different way. Then check the page yourself. Do not rely on one answer for a decision about money, health or law.

sections.heading: File and privacy basics
sections.body:
The file limit is 15 MB, and the tool works with PDF files only. The answers come from Google Gemini, which runs on Lazur's servers. Results can be copied with one click, so you can paste them into an email or notes app.

You do not need an account for your first 3 questions each day. Leave an email to get 3 more that day.

sections.heading: Chat with PDFs in any app on a Mac
sections.body: If you read PDFs every day on a Mac, Lazur works in any app: hold two keys and talk, and it types, answers or does the task where you are working.

sections.heading: What this tool is, and what it is not
sections.body:
This tool is not ChatGPT, and it is not made by OpenAI. It is a free chat-with-PDF page from Lazur. The answers come from Google Gemini, running on Lazur's servers.

It works in one way: you upload one PDF and ask questions about it. The answers come from that file. If the PDF does not contain the answer, the tool says so. It does not search the web or other files for you.

sections.heading: Chat with a PDF in ChatGPT itself
sections.body:
If you want to upload a PDF to ChatGPT, OpenAI's help center explains how file uploads work in ChatGPT. Menus and buttons change from time to time, so follow the current steps there rather than a copy of them here.

Search for 'File uploads FAQ' on help.openai.com to find the article. It covers which file types ChatGPT accepts and how uploads work for each plan. Read the version that is current for your account, because the rules change.

sections.heading: Use this free tool instead
sections.body:
If you want a quick answer from one PDF and do not want to sign in to a chat service, use the tool on this page.

1. Choose your PDF. It can be up to 15 MB.
2. Type your question in the chat box.
3. Read the answer. Check the page the tool names, if it names one.
4. Copy the answer with one click, or ask a follow-up.

You get 3 questions a day for free. Leave an email to get 3 more that day.

This is the right fit for a single document such as a contract, a manual, a research paper or a school handout. Upload it, ask what you need, and check the page the answer points to before you use it.

sections.heading: Limits and what they mean for you
sections.body:
This tool accepts PDF files only. For a Word or PowerPoint file, save it as a PDF first. The 15 MB limit applies to each file.

We did not confirm ChatGPT's current upload limits from OpenAI's help center while writing this page. If you need those numbers, check the official article or the upload dialog in your account, because they can change.

sections.heading: Tips for better answers
sections.body:
Ask one clear question at a time. Name the section or topic you care about. Ask for the page number when you need to check the source. If an answer looks too general, ask again with a keyword from the file, such as a heading or a name.

If you are comparing two tools, run the same PDF and the same question through each one, then check both answers against the page yourself. That check tells you more than any review.

faq.q: What is chat with PDF files?
faq.a: Chat with PDF files means asking questions about a document in plain language and getting answers from its text. You upload the PDF, ask a question, and read the reply. The answer should come from that file, not from outside sources.

faq.a: Upload a PDF of up to 15 MB to this page, type a question, and send it. The answer is generated by Google Gemini from the text of your file. Check the page the tool names before you rely on it.
